beats.beat: The company’s product range spans four categories: Functional Additives (FA), Chemically Modified Minerals (CMM), Soft Minerals (SM), and Hard Minerals (HM). These are used across diverse industries such as paints, plastics, cosmetics, and construction.

It does not have long-term contracts with customers or raw-material suppliers; sales are governed by purchase orders. Top 10 customers contributed 59%, 57%, and 59% of revenue in FY2015, FY2016, and FY2017 respectively.
Exports go to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, and Sri Lanka, totaling ₹1,068.18 lakh over the past five years.
The company derives substantial synergies from its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, which markets and sells the company’s products through its network.

beats.beat: Promoters are Mr. Chandresh S. Parikh, Mr. Atil C. Parikh, Mr. Rajesh C. Parikh, and 20 Microns Limited. They hold 89,48,270 shares – 99.76% of pre-issue equity.
Promoter Group (excluding promoters) holds 21,510 shares – 0.24%.
The company has related-party transactions with its promoter and group companies; details are in the financial statements (page 223). No auditor qualification mentioned for these.

Past instances of non-filing or delayed filing of statutory forms with RoC, paid with additional fees. Also, certain licenses for the manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia have not yet been obtained.

beats.beat: The Indian specialty chemicals industry (excluding agrochemicals and dyestuff) was estimated at ₹1,000 billion in FY2017 and is expected to grow at 12–14% CAGR, according to CRISIL Research.
The industry is highly fragmented, with SMEs holding 70–75% market share. Only a few Indian players can compete with global giants on innovation.

Growth drivers include rising domestic consumption, urbanisation, government initiatives like the Draft National Chemical Policy, and favourable global shifts (e.g., China’s stricter environmental norms reducing its specialty chemicals output).
Sub-segments like construction chemicals, water chemicals, and personal care ingredients are forecast to grow at 15% CAGR; textiles and flavours & fragrances at 12% CAGR.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals processes and sells specialty chemicals – Functional Additives, Chemically Modified Minerals, Soft Minerals, and Hard Minerals – and relies on a long-term marketing arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited.
The company is raising funds via an SME IPO on NSE EMERGE to set up a new manufacturing facility at GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, and for general corporate purposes.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who the company is, what it does, its promoter relationship, and the purpose of the IPO.

beats.beat: The issue is a fresh issue of equity shares; there is no offer for sale. The selling shareholder is not disclosed (only fresh issue).

Proceeds will be used for: (i) capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat; (ii) general corporate purposes; and (iii) creating a public trading market on NSE EMERGE.
The lead manager to the issue is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited; the registrar is Link Intime India Private Limited.

offer.heading: The IPO offer
offer.purpose: Detail the offer structure – fresh issue vs OFS, selling shareholder (if any), use of proceeds, and lead manager.

beats.beat: No long-term customer or supplier agreements: All sales are on purchase order, and raw material supply is not contracted. Losing a key customer or facing price spikes could hit revenue.
Negative cash flow in FY2017: Operating cash flow was -₹3.50 crore, which could signal working capital stress; sustained negative cash flow would impair growth.
Missing statutory licenses: The manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia, lacks required licenses and approvals; non-compliance could lead to penalties or shutdown.
Concentration on one customer network: Marketing and sales depend on the corporate promoter 20 Microns Limited. Any disruption in that relationship could severely affect revenue.
High promoter holding (99.76%) means low public float. Post-IPO, the free float will remain very small, which can lead to volatility and limited liquidity.
